questions.stem: From which phrase is the term FinOps derived?
questions.explanation: FinOps is a term derived from "financial operations".

questions.stem: What is the primary focus of FinOps?
options: Effectively managing the costs associated with cloud usage
Migrating on-premises servers to the cloud
questions.explanation: The primary focus of FinOps is managing cloud costs: understanding, optimising and controlling expenditure so it aligns with business goals.

questions.stem: What does the FinOps principle of shared responsibility mean?
options: Cloud providers share the cost of overspending with customers
Every team receives the same cloud budget
Financial considerations are a collective responsibility across organisational functions, not solely the finance department's
Engineering teams take over all financial reporting
Costs are split equally between finance and IT
questions.explanation: Shared responsibility means financial considerations are not solely the concern of the finance department but a collective responsibility across functions.

questions.stem: Which stakeholders does FinOps bring together to manage cloud costs?
questions.explanation: FinOps brings together stakeholders from finance, operations and IT/engineering to collectively manage and optimise cloud costs.

questions.stem: Which cloud service providers are named as examples of the infrastructure FinOps addresses?
questions.explanation: FinOps is tailored to cloud computing infrastructure such as the services provided by AWS, Azure or Google Cloud.

questions.stem: Why is FinOps described as a management practice rather than just a set of guidelines?
options: Because it involves a structured and ongoing approach to managing financial aspects of cloud operations
Because it is mandated by law in most countries
Because it is owned exclusively by senior management
Because it replaces the finance department
Because it applies only during annual budgeting
questions.explanation: Calling FinOps a management practice indicates a structured and ongoing approach to managing the financial aspects of cloud operations.

questions.stem: What is the ultimate goal of FinOps?
options: Enhancing efficiency and optimising cloud spending while balancing cost, performance and reliability
Maximising the number of cloud services used
Centralising all purchasing decisions in finance
questions.explanation: The ultimate goal of FinOps is to enhance efficiency and optimise cloud spending, balancing cost, performance and reliability.

questions.stem: How is FinOps characterised in terms of duration?
options: A one-time initiative completed at cloud migration
A project with a fixed end date
questions.explanation: FinOps is not a one-time initiative but a continuous improvement process in which teams regularly assess, analyse and refine their practices.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the educational component often included in FinOps?
options: To certify staff as cloud architects
To train finance staff to write code
To teach cloud providers about customer needs
To help teams understand how their decisions impact costs
To prepare teams for external audits
questions.explanation: Teams are educated about cloud financial management practices to enhance their understanding of how their decisions impact costs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a tenet of FinOps as described?
options: Cost management aligned with business goals
Financial decisions made solely by the finance department
questions.explanation: FinOps explicitly rejects the idea that cost is solely the finance department's concern; it promotes shared responsibility and collaboration.
